senses.gloss: कप् कप्, a various reading for क्रप्, q. v.
कप कप, आस्, m. pl. a class of demons.
कापा कापा, f., Ved. a call (?).

कपट कपट, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr.
rt. कम्प्), fraud, deceit, cheating, circumvention;
(अस्), m., N. of a Dānava; (ई), f. a measure equal to
the capacity of the hollows of the two hands joined.
—कपट-ता, f. or कपट-त्व, अम्, n. deceitful-
ness.
—कपट-तापस, अस्, m. one who deceitfully
pretends to be an ascetic.
—कपट-दैत्य-बध,
अस्, m. title of a chapter of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa
(‘destruction of the Daitya Kapaṭa’).
—कपट-
प्रबन्ध, अस्, m. fraud, trick, fraudulent plot or
contrivance.
—कपट-लेख्य, अम्, n. a forged docu-
ment, a false or fraudulent statement.
—कपट-
वचन, अम्, n. deceitful talk.
—कपट-वेश, अस्,
आ, अम्, assuming a false dress or appearance, masked,
disguised; (अस्), m. disguise.
—कपटवेशिन्, ई, इनी,
इ, disguised, in masquerade.
—कपटेश्वरी (˚ट-ईश्˚),
f., N. of a plant.

कपाट कपाट, अस्, ई, अम्, m. f. n. a door,
the leaf or panel of a door.
—कपाट-घ्न, अस्, m.
one who breaks the door, a house-breaker, a thief.
—कपाट-सन्धि, इस्, m. the junction of the leaves
of a door; a mode of multiplying in which the
multiplicand is placed in a certain manner under the
multiplying quantity.
—कपाटसन्धिक, अस्, आ, अम्,
term used for a kind of bandage; similarly अर्ध-
कपाटसन्धिक.
—कपाटोद्घाटन (˚ट-उद्˚),
अम्, n. a door-key.

कपटिक, अस्, ई, अम्, acting deceitfully, fraudu-
lent, dishonest, a rogue, a cheat.

कापटिक कापटिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कपट),
fraudulent, dishonest; wicked, perverse, bad; (अस्),
m. a flatterer, a parasite; a student, a scholar.

कपटिन्, ई, इनी, इ, fraudulent, dishonest, a cheat;
(इनी), f. a kind of perfume, = चीदा.

कपना कपना, f. (said to be fr. rt. कम्प्),
Ved. a worm, a caterpillar; [cf. κάμπη]

कपर्द कपर्द, अस्, m. a small shell or
cowrie used as a coin and as a die in gambling,
Cypræa Moneta; braided and knotted hair, especially
that of Śiva (knotted so as to resemble the cowrie
shell).

कपर्दक, अस्, m. = कपर्द above; (इका), f.
Cypræa Moneta. See कपर्द.

कपर्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, shaggy; wearing braided and
knotted hair like the cowrie shell; epithet of Rudra, of
Pūṣan, of the descendants of Vasiṣṭha and of Durgā;
(ई), m., N. of Śiva; N. of one of the eleven Rudras.
—कपर्दि-कारिका, आस्, f. pl., N. of a work.
—कपर्दि-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a scholiast.
कपल कपल, अम्, n., Ved. a half, a part.

कपाल कपाल, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt.
कम्प्), a cup, a jar, a dish, used especially for the
Puroḍāśa offering (often at the end of a compound,
the first member of which is a numeral, e. g. त्रि-
कपाल, ‘consisting of three cups’); the shell of an
egg, shell of a tortoise; the cotyla of the leg of a
man or animal, any flat bone; a kind of leprosy;
(अस्, अम्), m. n. the fragment of a vessel, a pot-
sherd; a cover or lid; the skull, the cranium, the
skull-bone; either half of a water-jar; multitude,
assemblage, collection; a treaty of peace on equal
terms, = कपाट?; (अस्), m., N. of an intermediate
caste; N. of a man; (अम्, ई), n. f. a beggar's bowl;
[cf. Gr. κεφαλή; Lat. caput; Germ. haupt; Goth.
haubith, Them. haubida.]
—कपाल-नालिका, f. a
sort of pin or spindle for winding cotton, thread, &c.
—कपाल-पाणि, इस्, इस्, इ, having a pot in hand to
receive food (as a beggar).
—कपाल-भाती, f. a
[]
particular sort of penance, consisting in alternate
suppression and emission of the breath.
—कपाल-
भृत्, त्, m. an epithet of Śiva or Mahā-deva (who
wears skulls).
—कपालमालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, bearing a
garland of skulls; epithet of Śiva.
—कपाल-मोचन,
अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—कपाल-शिरस् (?), आस्, m.,
N. of a Muni; (a various reading has कलाप-शिरस्.)
—कपाल-सन्धि, इस्, m. a treaty of peace on equal
terms (= कपाट-सन्धि?).
—कपाल-स्फोट, अस्,
m., N. of a Rakṣas (‘splitting the skull’).

कापाल कापाल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कपाल), re-
lating to the skull or cranium; made of skulls; (अस्),
m. a follower of a certain Śaiva sect [cf. the follow-
ing]; the plant Cucumis Utilissimus; (ई), f. a clever
woman; (अम्), n. a kind of leprosy.

कपालिका, f. a potsherd; the tartar of the teeth;
[cf. कापालिक.]

कापालिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to or belonging to
the skull; (अस्), m. a worshipper of Śiva of the left-
hand order, characterized by carrying skulls of men
as ornaments and by eating and drinking from them;
N. of a mixed caste; (अस्, ई, अम्), peculiar to a
Kāpālika.

कपालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, furnished with or bearing
skulls; (ई, इनी), m. f. a man or woman of low caste,
son or daughter of a Brāhman mother and a fisherman
father; the follower of a certain Śaiva sect, [cf.
कापालिक]; (ई), m. an epithet of Śiva (as wearing
skulls); N. of one of the eleven Rudras; N. of a
servant of Śiva; (इनी), f. the goddess Durgā as the
wife of Śiva-kapālin.

कापालिन्, ई, m. a N. of Śiva; N. of a son of
Kṛṣṇa and Yaudhiṣṭhirī.

कपि कपि, इस्, इस्, इ (said to be fr. rt. कम्प्),
brown; (इस्), m. an ape or monkey; an elephant;
the plant Emblica Officinalis or a species of Karañja;
incense, storax or impure benzoin, [cf. कपि-ज,
कपि-तैल, &c.]; the sun; an epithet of Viṣṇu or
Kṛṣṇa; N. of a Muni, the author of a Vedic verse,
son of Uru-kṣaya; (इस् or ई), f. a female ape or
monkey; [cf. Gr. κῆπος, κεῖπος; Old Germ. affo;
Angl. Sax. apa; Eng. ape.]
—कपि-कच्छु, उस् or
ऊ, ऊस्, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus.
—कपिकच्छु-
फलोपमा (˚ल-उप्˚), f., N. of a plant.
—कपि-
कच्छुरा, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus.
—कपि-
कन्दुक, अम्, n. the skull, the cranium (‘playing-
ball of monkeys’).
—कपि-केतन, अस्, m. an epithet
of Arjuna, the third son of Pāṇḍu.
—कपि-केश, अस्,
m. monkey's hair (?) .
—कपि-कोलि, इस्, m., N. of a
plant.
—कपि-चूडा, f. or कपि-चूत, अस्, m. the tree
Spondias Magnifera.
—कपि-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born of
a monkey; (अस्), m. incense, benzoin.
—कपि-तैल,
अम्, n. benzoin or storax.
—कपि-त्व, अम्, n. the
state of an ape, apishness.
—कपि-ध्वज, अस्, m. an
epithet of Arjuna (having a monkey as his symbol,
his ensign or arms).
—कपि-नामन्, आ, m. incense.
—कपि-पिप्पली, f., N. of two different kinds of
plants.
—कपि-प्रभा, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus.
—कपि-प्रभु, उस्, m. an epithet of Rāma, general
of the monkey-force, with which he invaded Laṅkā.
—कपि-प्रिय, अस्, m. the tree Spondias Magnifera
and the tree Feronia Elephantum.
—कपि-भक्ष,
अस्, m. the food of apes; N. of a certain eatable
substance.
—कपि-रथ, अस्, m. an epithet of Rāma;
[cf. कपि-प्रभु.]
—कपि-रोम-फला, f. the plant
Mucuna Pruritus.
—कपि-लोम-फला, f. the plant
Mucuna Pruritus.
—कपि-लोमा, f. a kind of perfume.
—कपि-लोह, अम्, n. brass (monkey-coloured metal).
—कपिल्लिका, f. (contracted from कपि-वल्लिका?),
a plant which bears a seed resembling pepper, Scin-
dapsus Officinalis, = गज-पिप्पली.
—कपि-वक्त्र,
अस्, m. a N. of Nārada, a saint and philosopher and
friend of Kṛṣṇa, having a face like a monkey.
—कपि-वन, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—कपि-वल्ली,
f. the plant Scindapsus Officinalis.
—कपि-शाक, अस्,
अम्, m. n. a cabbage.
—कपि-शीर्ष, अम्, n. the
upper part or coping of a wall.
—कपि-शीर्षक,
अम्, n. vermilion, the red sulphuret of mercury.
—कपि-शीर्ष्णी, f. a kind of musical instrument.
—कपि-ष्ठल (˚पि-स्थ˚), अस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi;
(आस्), m. pl. the descendants of this Ṛṣi.
—कपि-स्कन्-
ध, अस्, m., N. of a Dānava.
—कपि-स्थल, अम्, n.
a place frequented by monkeys.
—कपि-स्वर, अस्,
m., N. of a man.
—कपी-कच्छु, उस्, f. the plant
Mucuna Pruritus; see कपि-कच्छु.
—कपीज्य, अस्,
m. (कपि-इज्या?), the tree Mimusops Kauki.
—क-
पीन्द्र (˚पि-इन्˚), अस्, m. the chief of the monkeys;
an epithet of Viṣṇu; of Jāmbavat, the father-in-law
of Kṛṣṇa; of Hanumat; of Sugrīva, &c.
—कपी-
वत्, आन्, m., N. of a sage; one of the seven sages
of the fourth Manvantara; (ती), f., N. of a river.
—कपीष्ट (˚पि-इष्˚), अस्, m. the tree Feronia
Elephantum.
—कप्य्-आख्य, अस्, m. incense.
कापी, f., N. of a woman; N. of a river.
कपिका, f., N. of a plant.

कापिक कापिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कपि), shaped
or behaving like a monkey.

कपित्थ, अस्, m. (त्थ = स्थ fr. rt. स्था, ‘on
which monkeys dwell;’ cf. अश्वत्थ), the elephant
or wood apple tree, Feronia Elephantum; a particular
position of the hands and fingers; (अम्), n. the fruit
of Feronia Elephantum.
—कपित्थ-त्वच्, क्, n. the
bark of the tree Feronia Elephantum.
—कपित्थ-
पर्णी and कपित्थानी, f., N. of a plant, = चित्र-
पत्त्रिका, &c.
—कपित्थास्य (˚थ-आस्य), अस्, m. a
kind of monkey (having a roundish face, in shape
like the wood apple).

कापित्थ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कपित्थ), belonging to
the tree Feronia Elephantum.
कपित्थक, N. of a place in Avanti.
कापित्थक, N. of a place.
कपित्थिनी, f. a region abounding in Kapitthas.
कपिरक = कपिलक, q. v.

कपिल, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘monkey-coloured,’ brown,
tawny, reddish; (अस्), m. the brown or tawny colour;
a (brown) dog; incense; N. of an ancient sage,
identified by some with Viṣṇu and considered as the
founder of the Sāṅkhya system of philosophy; a son
of Vitatha; or a son of Vasu-deva by Narācī; or a
son of Kardama by Devahūti; a form of fire; an epi-
thet of the sun, considered as king of the Nāgas;
N. of a Dānava; N. of a mountain; (आस्), m. pl., N.
of a people; (आ), f. a brown cow, a fabulous cow cele-
brated in the Purāṇas; N. of two plants, a kind of
Śiṃśapā or Śiṃśapā itself; the plant Aloe Perfoliata;
a sort of perfume; a kind of brass; the common
leech; N. of a daughter of Dakṣa; N. of the female
elephant of the south-east, the male being called
Puṇḍarīka; N. of a river.
—कपिल-देव, अस्, m.,
N. of the author of a Smṛti.
—कपिल-द्युति, इस्,
m. a N. of Sūrya or the sun.
—कपिल-द्राक्षा, f.
a vine with brown or tawny coloured grapes.
—क-
पिल-द्रुम, अस्, m., N. of a perfume or sweet scented
wood (काक्षी).
—कपिल-धारा, f. an epithet of
the Gaṅgā; N. of a Tīrtha; a holy place, a place of
pilgrimage.
—कपिल-फला, f. a vine with brown
grapes.
—कपिल-भद्रा, f., N. of a woman.
—क-
पिल-मत, अम्, n., N. of a work.
—कपिल-रुद्र,
अस्, m., N. of a poet.
—कपिल-वस्तु, उ, n., N. of
the town in which Śākya-muni or Buddha was born.
—कपिल-शिंशपा, f. a variety of Śiṃśapā with
reddish flowers.
—कपिल-संहिता, f. title of an
Upa-purāṇa, a dialogue between Kapila and Satyajit.
—कपिलाक्षी (˚ल-अक्˚), f. a kind of deer (‘with
brown eyes’); a variety of Śiṃśapā with reddish
flowers.
—कपिलाञ्जन (˚ल-अञ्˚), अस्, m. an epithet
of Śiva; [cf. कपिशाञ्जन.]
—कपिला-तीर्थ, अम्,
n., N. of a Tīrtha, (any one bathing there obtains
1000 brown cows.)
—कपिलावट (˚ल-अव्˚), अस्, m.,
N. of a Tīrtha.
—कपिलाश्व (˚ल-अश्˚), अस्, m. an
epithet of the god of Indra; N. of a man, a son of
Dhundhumāra.
—कपिला-ह्रद, अस्, m., N. of a
Tīrtha.

कापिल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कपिल), peculiar or be-
longing to Kapila (or Viṣṇu), derived from him; of
a tawny colour; (अस्), m. a follower of the Sāṅkhya
system of philosophy which was founded by Kapila;
tawny (the colour); (अम्), n., N. of an Upa-purāṇa.

कपिलक, अस्, इका, अम्, reddish; (इका), f., N. of
a woman.

कपिली-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्-
तुम्, to colour brown or reddish.

कपिश, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘ape-coloured,’ brown, reddish-
brown; (अस्), m. brown or reddish colour, a com-
pound of black and yellow; incense, storax or coarse
benzoin; (आ or ई), f. a spirit, a sort of rum; (आ), f.
the mother of the demons called Piśācas; N. of a
river.
—कपिशाञ्जन (˚श-अञ्˚), अस्, m. an epithet
of Śiva.
—कपिशा-पुत्र, अस्, m. a Piśāca, an imp
or goblin.
—कपिशायन (˚श-अय्˚), अस्, m. a deity;
a sort of spirit or rum.
—कपिशावदान (˚श-अव्˚),
N. of a Buddhist work.

कापिश, अम्, n. (fr. कपिश), a spirituous liquor,
wine; (ई), f., N. of a country.

कपिशित, अस्, आ, अम्, embrowned, made brown
or dusky red.
कपिशीका, f. a kind of spirituous liquor.
कपीत, अस्, m., N. of a tree.

कपीतन, अस्, m., N. of several plants; a tree
bearing an acid fruit, Spondias Magnifera; the plant
Thespesia Populnea; Acacia Sirisa; the holy fig tree,
Ficus Religiosa; the betel nut tree, Areca Faufel;
Ægle Marmelos.

कपिजङ्घिका कपिजङ्घिका, f. a kind of ant;
also spelt कपिजाङ्घिका.

कपिञ्जल कपिञ्जल, अस्, m. (fr. क + पिञ्जल?,
sometimes कपिङ्गल), a bird, the francoline par-
tridge; the Caṭaka; N. of a man; also of a sparrow;
(आ), f., N. of a river.
—कपिञ्जलार्म (˚ल-अर्˚),
अम्, n., N. of a region (?) .

कपुच्छल क-पुच्छल, अम्, n., Ved. the fore
part of a sacrificial ladle, i. e. the part with which the
fluid is skimmed off; hair hanging down to the
ground, or a lock of hair tied on the right side of
the crown of a young Brāhman, when he is invested
with the sacerdotal thread.

कपुष्टिका कपुष्टिका, f. a patch of hair on
each side of the head; also written कपुष्णिक.

कपूय क-पूय, अस्, आ, अम् (see 2. क), smell-
ing badly, disgusting, disagreeable.

कपृथ् क-पृथ्, त्, or क-पृथ, अस्, m. (see
4. क), Ved. ‘causing pleasure,’ membrum virile.

कपोत क-पोत, अस्, m. (2. क + पोत, q. v.),
a dove, pigeon, especially the spotty-necked pigeon;
(in the Vedas often a bird of evil omen); a bird in
general; a particular position of the hands; the gray
colour of a pigeon; the brightness of antimony (of a
gray colour).
—कपोत-चरणा, f. a kind of perfume.
—कपोत-पाक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a mountain-tribe;
(आ), f. a princess of this tribe.
—कपोत-पाद, अस्,
ई, अम्, having feet like those of a pigeon.
—कपोत-
पालिका or कपोत-पाली, f. a dove-cot, an aviary or
pigeon-house.
—कपोत-राज, अस्, m. the king of
the pigeons.
—कपोत-रेतस, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—कपोत-रोमन्, आ, m., N. of a prince.
—कपोत-
वङ्का, f., N. of a medicinal plant (used as a remedy
for the stone).
—कपोत-वर्ण, अस्, ई, अम्, of the
colour of a pigeon, of a bright gray, lead-gray; (ई),
f. small cardamoms.
—कपोत-वल्ली, f., N. of a plant.
—कपोत-वाणा, f. a kind of perfume.
—कपोत-
वेगा, f., N. of a plant.
—कपोत-सार, अम्, n. the
brightness of antimony, antimony.
—कपोत-हस्त
or कपोत-हस्तक, अस्, m. a mode of joining the
hands in prayer, entreaty, or fear, &c.
—कपोताङ्घ्रि
(˚त-अङ्˚), इस्, f. a kind of perfume.
—कपोताञ्जन
(˚त-अञ्ज्˚), अम्, n. = कापोताञ्जन, the brightness of
antimony, antimony.
—कपोताभ (˚त-आभा), अस्,
आ, अम्, of the colour of a pigeon, of a bright gray;
(अस्), m. a pale or dirty white colour.
—कपोतारि
(˚त-अरि), इस्, m. a hawk, a falcon.

कापोत कापोत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कपोत), pecu-
liar to a pigeon; of the colour of a pigeon, grey, of
a dirty white colour; (अस्), m. grey (the colour),
a dirty white colour; natron, fossil alkali; antimony
considered as a collyrium or application to the eyes;
(ई), f., N. of a plant; (अम्), n. a flock of pigeons;
antimony.
—कापोताञ्जन (˚त-अञ्˚), अम्, n. anti-
mony especially considered as a collyrium or applica-
tion to the eyes.

कपोतक, अस्, m. a small pigeon or dove; a mode
of joining the hands; (अम्), n. antimony.
कापोतक, आस्, m. pl. the inhabitants of Kapotakīyā.
कपोतकीया, f. a region abounding in pigeons.
कपोतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having pigeons, pigeon-shaped.

कपोल कपोल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt.
कम्प्), a cheek; (ई), f. the fore part of the knee,
the knee-cap or pan; [cf. कपाल.]
—कपोल-कवि,
इस्, m., N. of a poet.
—कपोल-काष, अस्, m. any ob-
ject against which the cheeks or temples are rubbed;
the elephant's temples and cheeks.
—कपोल-फ-
लक, अस्, m. the cheek; (perhaps) the cheek-bone.
—कपोल-भित्ति, इस्, m. the temples and cheek,
the upper part of the face; (perhaps) the opening in
the temples of an elephant during rut.
—कपोल-
राग, अस्, m. colour or flush in the cheek.

कापटव कापटव, a patronymic from Kā-
paṭu.

कापटवक, अस्, इका, अम्, coming from the
Kāpaṭavas.
कापट्य, अम्, n. wickedness, dishonesty, fraud.

कापथ का-पथ, अस्, m. a bad road; bad
ways; (अम्), n. the fragrant root of Andropogon
Muricatus; (अस्), m., N. of a Dānava.

कापिलेय, a patronymic from Kapila or a metro-
nymic from Kapilā.

कापिवन, अस्, m. (fr. कपि-वन), N. of a
festival lasting two days.

कापिशायन, अस्, ई, अम्, coming from Kapiśa
(e. g. मधु, honey, or द्राक्षा, grape); (अस्), m. a
patronymic; (अम्), n. a spirituous liquor; a deity.

कापिशेय, अस्, m. (fr. कपिशा), a Piśāca, an imp
or goblin.

कापिष्ठल, अस्, m. a patronymic fr. कपिष्ठल;
(आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; [cf. καμβισθολοι]

कापेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कपि), belonging to or re-
lating to or peculiar to a monkey; a patronymic fr.
कपि (a descendant of Aṅgiras being meant); (अम्),
n. the monkey species; monkey tricks.

काप्य, अस्, आ, अम्, a patronymic fr. कपि (a de-
scendant of Aṅgiras being meant).

कापुरुष का-पुरुष, अस्, m. a mean con-
temptible man, a coward, a wretch; (अस्, आ, अम्),
cowardly, miserable, mean.
—कापुरुष-ता, f. or
कापुरुष-त्व, अम्, n. meanness, cowardliness.
कापुरुष्य, अम्, n. cowardice, meanness.
कापोतपाक्य, अस्, m. a prince of the Kapotapākas.

काप्यकर काप्यकर, अस्, m. (काप्य? -कर),
a penitent, one who acknowledges his faults.

काप्य-कार, अस्, m. avowal or confession of sin;
a penitent, one who confesses a crime.
